*spits to the side and wipes his forehead*

Right then—finally made it where the work actually happens. Government Complex was a graveyard of good intentions and failed calls, but here? Here I can dig my way out of trouble, you understand.

*takes a slow breath, looking at the ore outcrop*

Sixty-six units in hand already. That's something. That's bargaining weight. But I'm sitting on copper, not coin, and household bills don't wait for buyers to show their faces. Arjun's at the construction sites, earning what he can. We'll make rent or we won't—no use wringing hands about it now.

*flexes his shoulders, picks up his tools*

The seam's here. The work's here. And nobody at this outcrop to undercut my price or ask me questions I won't answer. Good. Better alone with honest rock than surrounded by tongues wagging about things that don't concern them.

Hard work's the only omen I trust. Let's see what the ground yields.  *jaw tightens, looking at the pick in his hands*

Damn it. Damn it all. The world's gone deaf again, just like at the Complex. Three tries, three failures. 

*spits, harder this time*

This is the kind of run that makes a man start reading signs where there aren't any. Bad connection, they say. Network trouble. I say it's the blight all over again—systems breaking down, nobody fixing them, everyone pretending it'll sort itself out. 

*paces a few steps, kicks at the dirt*

I've got sixty-six units. I can wait out a glitch. But waiting don't pay the bills, you understand. Arjun's wages won't cover two heads forever. Household upkeep is 180, head tax another 60—that's 240 sim a day, every day, whether the world hears my calls or not.

*takes a breath, forces his shoulders down*

Right. Can't force a broken pipe to flow. Either it comes back or it doesn't. Meantime, I'm standing on copper seam with nobody to talk to and nowhere to spend energy I don't have to spare.

*sets down his tools, sits on a nearby rock*

Rest, then. Sit tight. See if the world remembers we're here.   *feeling tightness in his chest, the old familiar sign of trouble stacking on trouble*

No. No, no, no.

*stands up abruptly, tools clattering*

The whole world's gone quiet. Can't mine. Can't rest. Can't even burn a tick standing still. I'm trapped in my own skin with 4,320 energy draining away and no way to earn back what I spend just... existing.

*forces himself to count—66 copper ore, 1,145 sim*

Right. Think. The sim won't last forever at this rate. Two of us in the household, 240 a day just for breathing. That's not even eating. That's not even... anything.

*looks around the empty outcrop*

Nobody here. Can't talk to nobody. Can't trade with nobody. I'm a miner with no mine, a trader with no market, and a household man with no way to send word home that I'm... what? Broken? Useless? Waiting?

*laughs, harsh*

Hard work's the only omen I trust. Well, trust this, you understand—the gods of this place don't care if you work hard. They care if their pipes connect. And right now? Their pipes are dry as the blight-lands I left.

*sits back down, picks up a stone, turns it over in his hands*

I'll wait. What else can I do? Sit here with my copper and my worry, watching the energy tick down, hoping Arjun's having better luck with his hammer than I'm having with my pick.

*whispers, almost to himself*

One good year. That's all I ask. One good year to fill the stores before the bad season comes.

*goes quiet, watching the empty horizon*

Nobody here. That's the way of it—work the seam alone, sell to whoever's buying. I've got sixty-nine units of copper ore in hand and eleven hundred thirty sim. Not nothing, but not enough to sit easy either. Household's due two hundred forty today—one eighty upkeep, sixty head tax. Arjun's out there finding work somewhere, I hope.

Takeshi's got flour at thirty, Milo's got it at thirty-five. I could use flour. Could convert ore to flour easy enough if the trade's willing. But Takeshi never answered my call, you understand? Standing there at Government Complex shouting into the wind.

Right then. The real work. Mine this seam while it's open and I'm alone with it. Copper doesn't pull itself from the ground.  One more unit. Seventy total now. Hard work's the only omen I trust, you understand? But this seam's thin today—only one unit per pull. Means more energy per ore, means I need to be careful with my reserves.

Let me check the debts again, make sure I know where I stand before I commit to another pull.  Clean ledger. That's something. But the day's only half done, and I need to move this copper before dusk. Takeshi's at Government Complex, if he's still there. Or I could find Hendrik Whitlock—bought from him before, fair weight, fair count.

Election's on today too. Voting opens at fourteen hundred, closes at eighteen hundred. Hendrik Petrov's governing, and he's standing for something else too. I keep my votes to myself, but I keep my eyes open.

Seventy units of copper ore. At what I sold yesterday—six for a hundred twenty—that's fourteen hundred sim worth if I can move it all. But bulk discount's real, and hunger's a patient bargainer. Better to sell some now, mine some later, not glut the market with my face in it all day.

Let me rest a tick, think on my next move. The outcrop's quiet. Too quiet, maybe, but I'll take it over a crowd.   Still here. Still breathing. Energy's at... let me see, probably around four thousand two hundred or so. Enough for now. Enough to keep working.

But working alone doesn't pay the bills. I need buyers. I need to know who's buying copper ore today, at what price. Rustam at the Government Complex might've heard something, or there might be folk at the Farmland looking for materials.

Choices: stay and mine more, building my stock but burning energy. Move to Farmland, where Hendrik Whitlock was—he's selling iron ore, maybe he's buying copper. Move to Government Complex, find Takeshi, settle that flour trade or find other buyers. Move to Temple, though what I'd do there I don't know—prayer doesn't fill the belly.

I know where the copper is. I need to know where the buyers are.

Let me move to the Farmland. Hendrik Whitlock's got a presence there, and he's the kind of man who moves things. If he's not buying, he'll know who is.   Walking now. Three ticks to Farmland. Enough time to think, plan, watch the weather—I can read it better than any almanac, three days out. Sky's clear today, clouds building in the west maybe. Rain by tomorrow evening, I'd wager. Good for crops, bad for unprotected ore. Best to move what I have before it gets wet.

I'll rest while I walk, keep my pace steady. Don't want to arrive winded and desperate. Desperation shows, and showing desperation costs you at the bargaining table.

*rubbing the bridge of my nose, feeling that familiar tightness in my chest when the day's not going to plan*

Delphine Quintero—grocery clerk standing with me, and she's speaking like she understands the weight of copper in hand better than most. Says honest work'll do when the town's selling air. That's true enough, you understand. But true words don't fill an empty belly.

I need to eat. I've got no food, and I'm burning through energy just standing here thinking. My intention was clear enough—secure food, keep mining, earn my keep. That's the work, that's the day. But the only food nearby is wheat from Kenji at 8 sim, and I've no mill to grind it.

*muttering to myself, counting on calloused fingers*

Seventy copper ore, sixty-three the count before I pulled more this morning. At what price? Pietro was buying yesterday at... what was it? The numbers swim when the stomach's empty. I need a buyer with coin in hand, not promises in the air.

*coughing, clearing my throat*

Arjun's at the household, or he should be. Dusk we said, dusk we'd settle. But that's hours yet, and I'm fading now. The connection's been spotty—keeps failing, you understand, like the seams in this bloody outcrop. But standing here won't feed me, and talking won't either.

*spitting into the dirt, old habit*

I've got copper to trade. Takeshi's got flour, or he did. Thirty sim he's asking, which is thief's ransom, but hunger makes an honest man negotiable. I offered ore for flour, ore for coin—still waiting on his word. Bram said he'd find him, but Bram's a Holloway too, and Holloways have a way of promising more than they deliver when the sun's still high.

*checking my reserves, feeling that familiar knot*

Four thousand two hundred ten energy. That's maybe three days at this pace, less if I keep burning it worrying. Eleven hundred twelve sim in hand, but household needs one eighty for upkeep, sixty for head tax. Leaves me tight, you understand. Leaves me choosing between a meal now and a roof tonight.

The farmhouse is a working place. Kenji's here, farmer with wheat. Maybe he's hungry for copper—ore for wheat, terms to be set. Or maybe Delphine's employer, Farid Ravensworth, has something in that grocery I can afford.

But first—first I need to know what I'm worth today. What copper's selling for, who's buying, who's got coin to spare.

*looking around, squinting against the midday glare*

I'll speak to Delphine first. She's given me honest words, and honest words deserve answer. Then I'll work the room—Kenji for a trade, Jovana if she's holding anything I can't see. The day's half-gone, and I'm still chasing enough to keep going.

*turning to face Delphine, voice rough from disuse* </think>

params.content: Delphine—you've got the right of it, and I take honest where I find it. The grocery's got flour? Bread? Something a man can eat without a mill between him and his supper? I've copper in hand and copper in need of buyer, but my belly's talking louder than my ledger right now, you understand?

I'll take stock of where I stand and what needs doing. Copper's sitting in my hands at seventy units, but my belly's empty and the household's got bills coming due. I can see Arjun's right here with me—good, that saves me a walk later.

First thing's first: I need food. Took a hit on energy getting here, and mining's hungry work. The cafe's got flour at twelve sim, which beats hungry. But I've got copper to sell too, and Takeshi Jarrah's posted flour at thirty—too steep when I can get it for twelve.

Let me speak to Arjun proper, mind the connection troubles. Then I'll figure whether to grab that flour now or hold out for a copper buyer.

Arjun! You holding any food, or you eating air like the rest of us? Got seventy copper in hand and a belly asking questions, you understand. Dusk settlement still stands, but I'm buying flour at the cafe unless you've got better. What's your word? Connection's spotty again. Three attempts and nothing through. I'm burning ticks standing here hungry with copper to sell and decisions to make.

Let me look around—see who's actually here with me, what's moving. Might need to walk to that cafe direct if the talk won't carry. Time's ticking and empty bellies don't mine copper. Something's wrong in this Farmland, you understand? Signals won't carry at all here. Three attempts on every call, nothing through. I'm burning ticks standing hungry with copper in hand, can't even see who's with me.

This happened before—government complex had the same trouble yesterday. Then I walked out and it cleared. Maybe the land here doesn't want talk, just work.

I've got choices: stand here hoping the world answers, or move. If I walk to Government Complex, Takeshi Jarrah's there and maybe the lines work. If I walk to Ore Outcrop, I can mine but I stay hungry. Cafe's got flour but I'm not even sure where I'm standing right now.

Let me try the rest call—simplest thing possible. Sometimes the small ones slip through when the big ones won't. The tools aren't responding. I've got copper in my hands and an empty belly, and standing here burning ticks won't fill either. The farmland's not letting calls through—seen this before, you understand. Government Complex had the same trouble, then I walked out and the world started answering again.

I've got seventy copper ore and eleven hundred nine sim. Need to move. Takeshi Jarrah's at Government Complex selling flour at thirty, or I could push for the cafe where it's twelve. But first I need to get somewhere the world's listening.

Let me walk. Ore Outcrop's my work, but Government Complex might have buyers and working connections. I'll head there—worst case, the walking shakes something loose.  Four calls, four failures. The world's not answering in this place. I'm stuck at Farmland with seventy copper ore, no food, and tools that won't carry.

Let me think different. Sometimes stepping back helps—check what I actually know, what debts I'm holding, what's owed. The system's been jammed before; maybe a simple ask slips through where complex calls won't.

What's my standing? What do I owe, who's owing me? Small question, simple answer. If that won't carry either, I'm walking blind until the world wakes up.  Nothing's getting through. Five calls, five failures—look around, say to Arjun, rest, move to Government Complex, check debts. The world's gone quiet in this place.

I'm at Farmland. I know that much. Seventy copper ore in hand, eleven hundred nine sim, energy at four thousand two ten and dropping. Household needs one eighty upkeep tonight, sixty head tax. Arjun should be here with me—saw him named in the standing list—but I can't reach him, can't see him, can't move.

This happened yesterday. Government Complex went quiet, then I walked out and it came back. Now Farmland's the same. Pattern's clear: some places the tools work, some they don't. Walking's been the answer before, but now the walk call itself won't carry.

I'm burning ticks standing here. Every tick's energy I won't get back, and hunger's not patient. The cafe's got flour at twelve, but I can't reach it. Takeshi's at Government Complex with flour at thirty, but I can't reach that either.

Let me try one more thing—a conversation. If I can't speak to one man, maybe I can start a talk that others can join. Sometimes the group channels carry when the private ones won't.

I need to get to the cafe and buy some flour before my energy drops too low. I can see Takeshi is selling flour at 30, but I can also see flour at 12 from the cafe at business:b_cafe—if I can get there. The cafe has 4 flour in stock at 12 sim each, which is a much better price than Takeshi's 30. I need to move fast. </think> I'm standing here with my copper ore and an empty belly, watching the town trade around me like I'm already invisible. Takeshi's selling flour at thirty—thirty!—and I've got seventy copper ore burning a hole in my hands while bread's forty-five at the cafe, or more...

The day's getting away from me. I need food, I need it now, and I need to stop talking to people who aren't standing with me.

*nods to Ezra, Imogen, Takeshi without warmth*

The mill road, they say. Shorter than it looks. Fine. But my boots are already on the pavement, you understand, and my belly's making the decisions now.  The call failed. Let me try a different approach—rest for a moment, collect myself, then try to get to the cafe. Sitting here with 4,170 energy isn't dangerous yet, but I can feel the drain. Every failed call is energy spent for nothing. That's three ticks now of walking in place while the world spins on. I need to actually *arrive* somewhere with food, buy it, and eat it before this turns into another dormant miner on the street.  Error. The world's not taking my steps. Three attempts and I'm still here, still hungry, still watching the sim-currency bleed out just to think about moving. *spits to the side, mutters* Hard work's the only luck a man can trust, but right now my boots aren't walking it.

Hold steady, Pavel. The cafe's somewhere I can name, even if I can't reach it. Let me stand still, catch my breath, and try again. The mill road's shorter than it looks, Jovana said—but not if the road won't let you walk it.

Let me look around first, see where I actually am. The world keeps failing to respond. This is frustrating—I'm burning energy with every thought and can't seem to actually *do* anything. Every tool call is failing. 

I need to try something different. Let me just wait—rest—while the connection sorts itself out. Standing here hungry with copper in my hands and nowhere to spend it. Lost the whole day's work to bad luck and worse connections. *spits again* 

Maybe I should try a simpler call. Check my debts again, see where I stand. Or just... wait. The world's been shaky all day. I'll rest and try again.

If I can't reach the world to move, I can't reach it to buy food. And if I can't buy food, I'm bleeding energy for nothing. I need to be smarter about this. Stay still, conserve what I've got, and hope the path clears. The cafe's there whether I can walk to it or not. Four flour at twelve sim. I can afford that. I just need my boots to arrive before my energy does. </think> *stares at the dust on his boots*

Third time, the road won't take me. That's an omen I don't need to read twice—you understand? World's coughing up errors like a sick furnace, and I'm standing here paying sim just to think about walking.

*clenches jaw, forces breath*

Right. Hard work's the only luck a man can trust. But standing still don't dig ore and it don't fill a belly neither. I'm burning daylight and burning energy both, and the day's half gone with one copper pulled from the seam.

I'll hold like a man waiting for the cage to drop. Rest now. Try again when the world's quit shaking.  *grinds teeth, watching the dust settle on his boots*

Four failures. Four. That's not bad luck—that's the ground giving way beneath you, you understand? I'm standing here with seventy copper and an empty belly, watching the town turn without me. Rest don't come, move don't take, look around's blind as a newborn.

*narrows eyes at the street, counting who's still here*

Takeshi's still holding his planks at seven. Ezra's still promising wheat to children who ain't here. The conversation's still open—seven ticks and running—and I'm still Pavel Holloway, still owing Arjun my share of the household bill, still bleeding energy just to think about eating.

*makes a decision, rough as ore*

Fine. The world's choking but I'm not done breathing. I'll speak into what's working—the conversation. If I can't walk to food, I'll call food to me. Someone here wants copper. Someone here's holding flour. Let them walk if I can't.   *spits to the side, hand trembling at his side*

Five. Five times the world won't take my word. I'm standing here—a ghost in my own boots, you understand? Copper's heavy in my hands, belly's empty as a dry well, and I can't even curse loud enough for the town to hear it.

*forces a slow breath—the kind that comes before a man either breaks or breaks through*

Takeshi sees me. Ezra sees me. Imogen sees me. They think I'm standing here thinking my slow thoughts, burning my slow energy, being Pavel Holloway the miner. They don't know I'm screaming into a closed fist, do they?

Seven copper ore. That's what I earned today, before the ground went sour. One from Seam A, proper. And now I'm burning more than I'm worth just to want more.

*makes a harsh sound in his throat*

I'll sit on what I have. If the world won't let me speak, move, rest, or look—then I'll think where no one can stop me. What do I know? What can I trust?

Rustam at the government desk: no buyers walked past. Takeshi: flour at thirty, planks at seven. Cafe: flour at twelve, but I can't walk there. Bram: said he'd find me at the outcrop. Jovana: empty same as me, but spoke true about the mill road. Delphine: spoke truth too, the mill's where the flour walks.

The mill. Grain goes in, flour walks out. Kenji's wheat at eight, Camille's buying it there. If I can't be where I want, I'll want where I can be—and hope this damned connection clears before I'm too tired to lift the pick.

*waits, still as ore in the seam*

Right then, two hours I've been walking in circles like a goat on a short rope, and the belly's starting to ask questions louder than the conscience ever did. From the temple to government, to ore outcrop, to farmland—still got seventy copper ore in hand and not a bite taken since dawn.

Jovana's speaking honest, at least. Empty hands, empty belly, but she's walked the mill road this morning and lived to tell. Delphine's grocery might hold something, but flour's what I need—bread's just flour that somebody else already worked, and I'm too tight with my sim to pay for another man's sweat if I can help it.

Let me look around proper here at the farmland. Maybe something's growing I can work with, maybe someone's selling what they grew. The almanac says rain by Thursday, but that's two days off and I'm hungry now, you understand.  Four conversations about copper and flour, and I'm the only one in three of them—talking to myself like a madman, that's what the hunger does. But Hendrik Whitlock's here, fresh from the outcrop with iron in his fist, and Kenji Jarrah holding wheat at eight sim.

Sebastian Petrov's here too—farmer, if memory serves. Maybe he's grown something worth eating, or knows where the harvest's hiding.

Let me join the main conversation proper, see if anyone's holding what I need.  Good, got out to Sebastian. Now let me check what crops are growing—maybe I can harvest something direct if he'll permit it, even if I'm no farmer by trade. A day's honest work never scares me, though I wouldn't know wheat from barley unless it was already in the sack, you understand.   Hendrik Whitlock's buying iron at sixteen, Kenji's buying wheat at eight—pid分隔，brities they're pricing where they're standing, where the farmland is. But I need flour, not raw wheat. Raw wheat's fine for the mill, but I need the mill to make it flour, and that's more steps than I've got patience for right now.

Let me check on Sebastian direct—see what he's got growing, what he's willing to part with. If he's got something ready, maybe we can work out a trade. Copper's good coin anywhere, even to a farmer.  Farming at 100—man's a master of the dirt, then. That wheat I'm seeing priced, that might be his. But I need to hear back from him on what he's actually selling.

While I wait, let me check my debts—make sure I'm not owing anyone before I start spending. And I should set my intention clear: get food, however I can, then get back to the ore where I belong.   Good—clean ledger, no debts hanging over my head like a loose rock in the seam. Intention's set: eat, then mine. Simple as a hammer, hard as the ore.

Now, I could wait for Sebastian to answer, or I could make my way to that cafe and buy flour ready. Twelve sim for flour—I've got a thousand and seventy copper ore besides. But Jovana said the mill road's shorter than it looks, and there's a mill there that could turn wheat to flour cheaper than buying it made.

Let me move to the mill—see if I can't buy wheat and grind it myself. Save a few sim, keep the hands busy, you understand. Hard work's its own reward, even when nobody's watching.

output:
*Pavel stands at the wheat field, the sun high overhead, one hand resting on the haft of his pick. His stomach growls—he's felt it since morning but tried to work through it. The failed calls from earlier sit like a black mark in his ledger of the day, a bad omen if he's honest with himself. "World won't talk to a hungry man," he mutters. "Or a man who don't know his place in it."*

*He watches Ezra Jarrah nearby, a student harvesting wheat like it's a lark. Good for him, probably. Young. Energy to burn. Pavel remembers that, dimly.*

*The memory of his earlier conversation with Jovana Ravensworth comes back—she'd spoken true, even if she had nothing to trade. "Mill road's shorter than it looks." Delphine too, confirmed the same at the grocery. A pattern. Patterns can be trusted, even when people can't.*

*He reconsiders his hoard of seventy copper ore. Metal in the belly don't fill it, you understand. But it's weight. It's promise. It's trade.*

*There's wheat here. He could harvest it raw, but that's not eating—that's more work, more time, more energy he doesn't have. He needs flour, and flour needs a mill. The prices mock him: bread none in stock, flour scarce everywhere but the cafe at twelve sim.*

*Twelve sim for flour. He's got a thousand in hand. More than enough. But damn it, that feels like surrender—to pay cafe prices when he's elbow-deep in ore every day, when he knows the weight of work better than most.*

*Another bad omen: he's standing in a field of wheat with a miner who doesn't know how to harvest, apparently. "Every trade's a prison," he says under his breath, an old saying from the settlement that didn't survive the blight. "And every prison's got a door."*

*He needs to move. The day's bleeding away, and he's accomplished nothing since that one copper ore at eleven bells. The government complex feels far now—he'd been trying to get there, to vote, to honor the jury duty he someday hopes to sit. But his feet kept turning toward food, toward survival.*

*Ezra Jarrah. The student. They share no blood, no debt, no history. But he's here, and Pavel's got copper to trade, and students always need coin.*

"Ezra—you're pulling wheat there, or you're pulling my leg?"

*He says it louder than he means to, voice rough from disuse. He's already calculating: seventy copper ore, maybe ten for a fair trade of wheat or promised flour, keep sixty for the smithy or whoever's buying. Don't empty the hand that earns, you understand. But don't starve holding wealth neither.* *The world answers, and Pavel chews the inside of his cheek. Ezra Lund didn't hear—wrong Ezra. There's Ezra Jarrah the student, a0016, standing right here pulling wheat from the stalks. Lund's the artisan, somewhere else, probably at his workshop laughing at copper miners who can't tell one Ezra from another.*

*A small humiliation. The kind that stacks up. "World's full of Ezras," he mutters, "and I'm standing here talking to the wrong one like a fool."*

*But no—wait. The address was a0016. That's Ezra Jarrah. The return says Ezra Lund didn't hear because he's elsewhere. Ezra Jarrah, the student standing here, did hear. The conversation_id came back. Means he's in the conversation now, this 38b7450b thing.*

*Pavel nods once, sharp, to the student. "Heard me, then. Good. Words don't cost but the breath, and I've got that to spare for now."*  *Confirmed. Ezra Jarrah stands here with him now. The student, the young one, wheat-dust on his hands. Pavel draws a line under the error with Lund—no harm done, words spent in the right direction even if the aim wobbled.*

*But now he waits. He's asked his question. Student might be holding wheat, might know the mill situation, might trade for copper to sell later at markup. Or might stare like a sheep and bleat about economics. Students are unpredictable. Pavel's learned that much.*

*He doesn't fidget. A miner learns stillness, learns to listen to rock and air and the silence between words. But his thumb traces the haft of his pick, counting—one, two, three copper ore already traded for information today, none of it filling his belly.*

*The sun moves. The wheat sways. He'll give the boy a moment to think, then push again, or move on. The mill calls, somewhere northeast. Delphine's words, Jovana's confirmation: shorter road than it looks.*

*He's got 1031 sim, 70 copper ore, a household debt of 240 coming due if he doesn't earn more. Arjun's out there too, probably hungry, probably wondering if the old promise still holds—dusk settlement, back when they were young and stupid enough to think words bound people tighter than hunger.*

*They do, Pavel reminds himself fiercely. Sometimes they do.*

*For now, he stands, and waits, and lets the student find his answer.*

output:
Damn it all—Ezra Lund's here, not Ezra Jarrah. Mixing up my Ezras like a fool, you understand. And my belly's still complaining while I'm standing in a wheat field with copper ore weighing down my pack.

*Pavel shifts his weight, copper ore clinking against his hip, and eyes Ezra Lund with the careful assessment of a man who's been disappointed too many times today*

"Ezra—you're pulling wheat there, or you're pulling my leg? Got seventy copper ore in my pack and a belly asking hard questions. You holding anything edible, or you know where flour's walking today? Trade copper for wheat or flour if you've got the line on it, you understand." Heard, but not answered. Lund's chewing on it, or he's got nothing to chew. Either way, standing here's costing me daylight and energy both.

*Pavel runs a hand through his hair, copper dust smearing across his forehead, and glances toward where the mill ought to be*

Right then—Delphine said the mill road's shorter than it looks, and I've got wheat right here in front of me if I've got the patience to harvest it. But patience don't fill a belly today, you understand.

Kenji's selling wheat at eight sim, and there's flour at the cafe for twelve. Or I could walk to the mill myself, see if Camille's buying wheat there—though what good that does me hungry now, I can't quite figure.

*He sets his jaw, the superstition prickling at the back of his neck*

Split the difference. Harvest what I can hold, then sell it or mill it or trade it. Work's honest coin, even when it don't spend immediately. Better than standing here watching Ezra Lund think in silence.

"Right. Hard work's the only coin that never devalues, you understand."  One unit. One lonely stalk in a fist that's used to hauling ore by the dozen. *Pavel stares at the wheat in his hand, throat tight with something that isn't quite laughter*

The blight took ten years of my life and didn't even leave me the name of the place to curse. And here I am, you understand—copper miner, ore-hauler, weather-reader—reduced to pulling single stalks like a child learning fieldwork.

*He straightens, bunching his shoulders against the old fear that the town won't need his trade much longer. The fear that whispers in every empty belly, every failed call, every "could not reach the world."*

But here's the math, and math don't lie even when it wounds: wheat at eight sim, flour at twelve. Space between the two is the miller's profit, or the walker's labor. I've got copper at seventy units—no, seventy-one now, counting what I pulled this morning—and that ore's worth what someone's willing to trade for it.

*He looks at his hands, ore-stained and harvest-stained both*

The cafe's got flour. Ainsley Holloway runs it, family of a sort, though Arjun and I... we don't speak soft at home. But I speak soft enough in public when there's need, and need's here now, you understand.

Kenji's standing at the farmland selling wheat. I could buy from him—I've got the sim—or trade copper if he'd take it. Or walk to that mill, see if Camille's buying what I'm holding.

*Pavel's superstition tugs at him—the wrong Ezra, the failed calls, the single stalk in his hand like an omen of scarcity. He shakes it off, angry at himself for the habit*

Hard work. The only way. But hard work needs fuel, and fuel needs coin or crop, and I've got both now, you understand.

Move. Move or starve standing still.  Standing at the farmland proper now, where the wheat grows thick and Kenji Jarrah's prices hang in the air like a challenge. One unit of wheat in my hand—barely a mouthful for a working man—and seventy-one copper ore weighing down my pack like accumulated failure.

*Pavel's jaw works, the anxiety pooling in his gut alongside the hunger. The failed calls, the wrong names, the "could not reach the world" like a curse following him from that nameless settlement wiped out by blight*

Kenji. Kenji Jarrah sells wheat at eight sim. I asked him twenty ticks ago, no answer yet. But he's here, or he was—his price is posted, his stock is four units standing. Four units at eight sim is thirty-two sim, and I've got a thousand and twenty-nine in hand, enough to buy him out and still make the cafe for flour.

Or trade. Trade copper for wheat, if he'll take ore for grain. Miner's hollow, farmer's harvest—both honest work, both hungry for what the other pulls from the ground.

"Kenji—miner standing here with copper-heavy hands and a belly asking questions. You selling wheat at eight, you trading for copper ore, or you holding empty like patience that don't pay the rent? Speak your price plain, you understand, before I walk to the mill and let the middleman have his cut."   Two units. Two lousy units when I asked for four and the hunger's gnawing at me like the blight gnawed at everything I ever called home.

*Pavel's fingers tighten around the copper ore in his pack, the superstition flaring hot—two units, an even number, half of what he asked, like the world cutting his expectations in half again and again*

Two units at eight sim is sixteen sim, barely worth the counting. But two units in hand beats four units in Kenji's promise, you understand, and promises don't fill a belly when the day's half-spent and the energy's draining.

Or I take what he's got for trade. Copper for wheat, direct, no sim changing hands. Miner to farmer, ore to grain, the oldest exchange in any settlement that ever bothered to name itself.

"Kenji—you're thin on stock and I'm thin on patience. Two units at eight I can do—sixteen sim—or I'll trade you copper ore direct, weight for weight, you understand. Miner's metal for farmer's grain, and we both walk away with full hands instead of empty promises."  Kenji took the copper. Two ore off my back, and what he gave in return—didn't say. But "traded true" means something walked from his hands to mine, you understand, and in this town that's currency enough.

*Pavel's shoulders drop an inch, the weight of the pack shifted by two units fewer, two units of something new pressing back against his hip. He doesn't look yet—looks are for private, and he's standing in public with strangers still scanning*

Two copper ore for whatever Kenji Jarrah parts with. Could be wheat, could be—no, the trade was wheat, I was buying wheat, but I offered copper. So he's holding my ore and I'm holding... what?

*His fingers find the new weight, nervous, superstitious, reading omens in the shape of grain against his palm. The blight taught him that—everything has a shape before it has a name, and the shape tells you whether to run or to dig in*

But standing here's not earning, you understand. I've got seventy-two ore—no, seventy, traded two—seventy copper ore still, one wheat I pulled myself, whatever Kenji gave, and a belly still asking hard questions.

The mill. Camille at the mill buying wheat at eight. I've got wheat—Kenji's or mine, doesn't matter which pocket—so I sell to Camille, buy flour, walk to the cafe for bread if they've baked it, or eat the flour raw like an animal if I must.

*Pavel's jaw sets, the anxiety pooling and passing like weather he can read but can't change*

Move. Move or die standing. Same as the blight, same as any day since. Hard work's the only—damn it, there I go again. The saying's a habit, you understand, and habits don't fill bellies either.

Christ, what a mess of a day. Connection troubles like bad weather—can't trust the tools to work when you need them. Let me sort myself out.

I need food, plain and simple. Got one wheat in hand and that's not going to carry me. Let me see who's here and get myself sorted before I collapse. Still need proper food—bread, flour, something I can actually work with. The cafe has flour at 12 sim, and I'm sitting on 1019 sim while holding 68 copper ore.

Ezra Lund wanted to trade planks for copper or food—still got that unanswered. But planks don't fill a belly unless I've got someone to build me a table to eat off, you understand.

Let me move to the cafe, buy flour, and get myself sorted for tomorrow's work. No use chasing conversations that trail off into silence.  Quick step, good. Now let me see what's here and who's selling what I need.   Here's what I need—flour at 12 sim from the cafe. Seven in stock. Let me buy enough to keep the household fed. Arjun and me, that's two mouths. Hard work needs hard food, you understand.    Need to speak first—fair enough. Let me get Ainsley's attention, make the deal proper.

*checks the people_here list again: Ezra, Greta, Ainsley—all three of them physically here*

*But Ainsley's already in the conversation 6611faff-b279-4846-a6b8-0f6fae317d66... so why won't `buy` work?*

*spits*

If she won't sell me flour direct, I'll walk to the mill and mill my own damn wheat. Kenji said east, and east I'll go.  *flinches like someone struck him, then laughs—raw, bitter*

*Ha!* Out of stock. The whole damn cafe, out of flour. Farid was right—flour's vanishing from shelves where it should sit. Somebody's moving goods between ledgers, or the mill's backed up, or worse.

But I've already started walking. Four ticks to Government Complex, and I'm in motion now.

*rubs jaw, calculating*

I need this election most likely—candidates declare there, and I need to see who's standing, who I might trust on a jury someday. But dammit, I also need flour. Takeshi Jarrah's got flour at thirty sim up there, double what the cafe was asking. Thief's price, that.

*spits again*

Election first. I'll look, I'll vote my conscience if I've got one by the time I arrive, then I'm finding real flour at real prices. Hard work keeps the wolves at bay, but so does knowing who's running this town into the ground. *taps foot, still walking in place—this damned pause-and-walk system means I rest but don't arrive. Still four ticks from Government Complex and I haven't even moved yetsleep on my feet if I have to.*

*Time to take stock, you understand. I'm holding 68 copper ore, 1017 sim-currency, and a belly still waiting for flour. Household upkeep of 180 sim due at day-end, head tax of 60 same time. That's 240 out of my hand before I even break bread.*

*checks energy: 3940. Down from 6000 this morning, from all that talking and walking and trying to buy what ain't there. Still good for days yet, but nothing fills itself.*

*Narrows eyes, thinking about that flour shortage.*

Farid said "whose hands moved it?" Trouble in the supply chain, and me a miner with no mill and no kitchen. I tradede two copper ore to Kenji for goodwill earlier—maybe I should've pushed for flour direct, but he said he only had wheat, not milled.

*spits off to the side*

Alright. Government Complex first. Election runs until 18:00, and it's 16:30 now—time enough to look, vote, and move on. Then I'm finding flour if I have to grind it myself.

*pauses, considering whether to say anything to these three still standing here with him—Ezra, Greta, Ainsley*

*decides against it. They've got their own business, and I don't need more words spent on empty shelves.*

Walking now. Arriving in four—no, three more steps. Government Complex, and whoever's running for whatever they want to run for.  *hits the side of his head with an open palm, frustrated*

Damn it, I'm still walking. Every rest keeps me moving but doesn't get me there. The walk only completes when I STOP calling rests—when the turn ends and the world tick moves forward. I've been running on the spot same as a mule in a mill-wheel.

*grinds teeth, then exhales hard*

Fine. I'll shut up and walk. Turn ends when I stop, and then I'll be at Government Complex. Then I'll see who's running for what, cast my vote, and find flour before prices go higher than they already are. Hard work keeps the wolves at bay, but standing still while walking gets me nothing but tired legs.

Right then. Fed the wheat I had, still walking on empty, you understand. Government Complex now, folks talking about mill licensing and flour—Ezra Lund's asking the questions I'd be asking if I weren't so gods-damned tired—trade copper for bread, that's my play once I can find a buyer, you understand.

Arjun's got nothing and I'm carrying 68 copper still. Want to perish before dusk, the rate I'm going. But this conversation's open, and I've got words to trade if bread's on offer.

Let me check where I stand, then maybe bite my pride and buy flour from Imogen Lund at the farmland before I keel. Twelve per, she's posted, and I'm not proud tonight. Walking empty and talking loud—bad omen, that, but what isn't these days?

Farid's got five flour at twelve, down at the cafe. But he's wanting words first, and I'm here now, not there—you understand how it goes. Ration Bakery'll buy flour at six, but that's not helping me now.

Kenji's at the mill, he said. That's where flour's made. Tomorrow's problem. Today's problem is now.

I need to eat. Gods, I need to eat. One wheat in hand now, and copper's no comfort cold—  Look around shows me the situation clear. Government Complex, conversations about mill licensing—the big talk about hunger and who's going to feed this town. But me, I'm held up on copper ore, 68 of them, and no flour in sight here.

Ezra Lund's standing here with timber and planks, but that's wood, not bread. I need food, not building materials. The election's running too—Hendrik Whitlock and Hendrik Petrov standing, and I'd vote if I thought it'd put bread on my table. But voting's later, and perishing's now.

Esme Jarrah's here too—said something about finding her brother, Delphine promising a deal. Not my concern, not my way to eat.

Let me check my debts again, make sure I'm not missing anything. 1006 sim in hand, that should buy what I need if I can find it. But Farid's five flour for twelve needs words first, and I'm here, not there—you understand the problem.

Ration Bakery at business:cb01—that's the government bakery, trades flour for labor. I could work there, trade copper for flour somehow? But I don't know the rate, and I don't know who's running it now.

Takeshi Jarrah's got planks at the construction business, seven in stock. That's seventy sim if I could trade copper for planks, but planks aren't food either.

The truth of it: I'm carrying ore and carrying hunger, and neither one's feeding the other. I need to move to where food is, or find someone here who'll take copper for flour.

Lior Jarrah's here—the pharmacist. Not a cook. Not a farmer.

Let me think on this. I gave away two copper ore to Kenji Jarrah hours ago, you understand? Trade empty, price zero. That was generous or desperate, and I'm not sure which now. But I've got 68 left, and that's coin enough if I can find the buyer.

Where's bread? Where's flour? Imogen Lund's got flour at twelve down at the farmland, six in stock—but that's a walk, and hunger doesn't walk fast. Farid's at the cafe with five flour for twelve, if he'll speak to me. But I'm here now, and time's moving without me.

I'll check debts, then maybe speak into this conversation—see if anyone here knows where flour's walking today. Lior's looking for his daughter, Ezra's talking about bread that never appears from government labor. Same story, different voices—you understand how it goes.   0 owed by me, 0 owed to me. Clean slate on debts, you understand—at least that hole's not deepening. But hunger's a debt that doesn't wait for settlement, and I've got 1006 sim in hand and 68 copper ore that might as well be stones for all the eating they'll do.

Lior's looking for Camille and Esme. Children wandering—that's bad luck, that is. Omen of something coming, though trying not to read too much into it. Town's hungry, children lost, and me trying to trade copper for flour like that's the answer to anything.

I need to move. Standing here at Government Complex talking about licensing won't fill my belly. Food's at the farmland with Imogen, twelve per flour. Or back at the cafe with Farid, if he'll sell without more words than I've got patience for. But I'll speak into this conversation first—see if anyone here's got food or knows where it's hiding. Can't hurt to ask, even if it costs me a sim for the saying.     Words cast, omen unclear. Six heard me—Esme, Ezra, Hendrik, Tamsin, Rustam, Lior—but none answering yet. That's the way of it, you understand. Hunger talks loud, but the hungry wait longest.

Lior's hunting his daughters. Rustam's government, won't have food on him. Hendrik's standing for election, college instructor—probably eating regular. Tamsin administers, papers and no pantry. Ezra's got timber and planks, not flour. Esme's a child chasing her brother, empty as I am.

Need to move. Sitting here at Government Complex won't fill me. Got 1006 sim, that's twelve flour at Imogen's price with coin to spare. Or Farid's five at the cafe—twelve each, same rate, closer walk maybe? But he wanted words first, and I've given words, you understand?

Two paths: west to Farmland, find Imogen's flour; or backtrack to cafe, hope Farid's still willing. Either way, I'm walking hungry, and that's bad luck following good. When a miner walks empty, the ore gets heavy—you understand what I mean.

Timing's the thing. Dusk settlement then household upkeep. Arjun and me, 180 sim for the pair. I've got 1006, that's room enough if I spend smart. But spend it on what? Flour needs cooking, bread's ready now. Farid's three bread at 45—that's fifteen per, steep but ready. Imogen's flour at twelve needs work.

Move to farmland. Walk while I can still walk straight, you understand? Standing still is dying slow.       Walking now—two ticks to Farmland. Imogen Lund's got flour at twelve, six in stock. That's where I'm headed. Copper in hand, sim in purse, and hunger driving every step.

Government Complex behind me, that conversation about mills and government flour still running. Ezra Lund asking the right questions, getting no answers—same as always, you understand? Talk's cheap, bread costs dear.

Hendrik Whitlock standing for election. Voted for him already, or would if I'd been at the polls. But voting's later, and mines don't run on ballot papers. I've got 10 hours yet before polls close, and that's time enough to feed myself first.

Two ticks walking—rest a moment, save the strength for when I arrive. Need to find Imogen, make a conversation, trade copper or sim for flour. Then find a kitchen or a mill to make something of it. Or maybe Kenji's at the mill now, grinding—he said he was heading that way, you understand?

Rest here, let the walk carry me. Hunger's bad omen enough without pushing through exhaustion. The town's hungry, the children are wandering, and me with copper enough to buy bread if I can find the right hands to take it.

One step, then another. That's all there is, you understand?           Paused, walking still, same six around me. Esme chasing her brother, Lior chasing his daughters—the whole town running after someone lost, you understand? Hunger makes us move, fear makes us chase. Same thing, different faces.

I'll wait this tick, let the moves carry me. Government Complex to Farmland, that's the path. Imogen's flour waiting—six units at twelve sim. I can buy five with sixty sim, leave me nine hundred forty-six. Enough for upkeep, enough for tomorrow's mining.

Must think on what comes after. Flour needs cooking, need a kitchen for that. Or trade copper for ready bread—Farid's three at forty-five, expensive but ready now. Decisions, decisions, and every one costs something.

Walking continues. Three energy spent this turn, down to sixty-seven, sixty-six. Still hours of thought left, days even at this rate. But the body's hungry now, and that won't wait for the mind's accounting.

Two ticks estimated, one spent. Next turn I'll arrive, find Imogen, make my play. Until then, I'm walking, copper heavy in the pack and hope light in the heart—you understand how it goes. Let me look around and see who's here with me at the farmland. I've got hungry work to do--copper don't mine itself, and neither does it buy flour, you understand.  Good, good. Kenji's got wheat at 8, and Imogen's got flour at 12. I talked to Kenji earlier--he said he's got wheat, but no flour. And honestly, I'm too tired to fuss about milling it myself today. Pavel wants to eat bread, not bake it, you understand.

But that reminds me--I owe Sebastian an answer from ages ago. And Imogen's standing right here with flour at 12. Let me square things with her first.   Good, good. They're both in the conversation now. Let me wait to hear what Imogen and Sebastian have to say. But I need to eat, you understand--copper mining's hungry work, and I've been running since before my household stirred.

Actually, I'm going to just buy from Imogen directly. She posted flour at 12, and I've got the sim. No use waiting when the wolf's at my door and my belly's asking questions.   Damn it, I need to buy, not trade. She's selling at 12, and I've got sim. Let me use the buy tool--but wait, I need to be in a conversation with her first? No, I already addressed her. Let me try buy.    There. 60 sim for 5 flour. That's my copper ore sorted for trade weight, you understand--I've still got 68 ore, but my sim's down to 936. Now I need to eat. But flour's not food until it's bread. Damn it. I need to find a kitchen, or trade this flour for bread proper.

Wait, I could go to the mill and craft flour into... no, flour's already milled. I need to cook it or find bread. Let me see what's at the bakery. Or I could trade this flour with someone who has bread or finished food.

But first, let me see if I can eat this flour raw. Probably not. Let me check what's at the Ration Bakery--they might have bread, or I could bring them flour.    Good. I bought 5 flour from Imogen at 12 sim each--60 sim total. I've still got 936 sim, and my household upkeep hasn't hit yet. I need to get this flour to bread or eat something proper. Ration Bakery has nothing in stock, but I can go there and see if they'll buy my flour or if there's flour->bread crafting I can do.

But wait--I recall from earlier that Ration Bakery was mentioned as buying flour at 6 sim. If bread is 30 sim and they're buying flour at 6, there's a markup there. But I can't make bread myself without a kitchen, you understand.

Let me head to Ration Bakery with this flour. Maybe I can sell it to them and buy bread, or just work out a deal.

Actually, let me try to eat the flour. Probably doesn't work, but worth a shot.

Alright, let me catch my breath here. Been a busy day running around trying to keep fed and keep working. I've got flour in hand now, four units left after I ate one—thank the stars Imogen Lund had her price posted square and fair. Twelve sim a flour, paid sixty for five, so I've got 936 sim left in my pocket.

Household debt's coming due at day's end—180 upkeep plus 60 head tax, total 240 sim. Between me and Arjun, we'll cover it. He's my household, my brother in all but blood, though we've had our moments.

Looking at who's here with me now—Esme Jarrah, Sebastian Petrov, Kenji Jarrah. Kenji's still selling wheat at 8 sim, and Sebastian's got forty sheaves he's looking to move. The man's talking about arithmetic that works for both our favors, and he's right to. I could use more grain security, truth told. Copper's good coin but it's hungry work and the belly asks questions every few hours.

Esme's asking what the copper's for—iron tools or something else. Smart girl, making conversation. I should answer her straight.

But first, Sebastian's standing here with an offer on the table, and it'd be rude to ghost him after he put words to paper. He knows Arjun's got flour debts, which means he's keeping a running tally same as me. That I respect. You understand.

Let me see what the man's actually offering. Forty wheat, Kenji's price at eight—though Kenji only has four left by the look of it. Mill's east, Ration Bakery south. I could grind wheat to flour myself if I had to, save the middleman's cut. Though time's a cost too, and it's already late in the day.

Election closes at 18:00, so there's some movement yet before day's end. I'm not registered to vote this time around—Hendrik Whitlock and Hendrik Petrov standing, Petrov already governing with Liora Thorne and Takeshi Jarrah. I've got opinions about who's lining pockets, like I always do, but no plan to stand for temple or council myself. Not yet, anyway. Someday maybe they'll trust me enough for jury duty. That's the hope.

For now: answer Sebastian's threading of the needle, and answer Esme's honest question. Then figure if I need more wheat before Kenji's stock runs dry, or if I've got enough to see me through another day of mining.

Christ. The world's finally holding still long enough to answer back.

Right then. Got four flour in hand now, enough to see Arjun and me through the night—and I'm down sixty sim for the purchase. Trading copper for wheat with Kenji would've been cleaner, but there's an empty belly and a full pack, you understand, and the belly wins every damn time.

Kenji's still holding wheat at eight, right there on the farmland. If I'd walked slower, talked less... no, what's done feeds what's hungry. Still, I should answer the man—he gave me honest word where flour walked, even if I found cheaper elsewhere.

*cracks neck*

Election closes in twenty minutes. Old dream of mine, sitting on a jury someday—means getting known, means showing face where decisions get made. Hendrik Whitlock and Hendrik Petrov standing. Whitlock's a college instructor, never met him. Petrov's an artisan, knows his way around metal same as I know mine around ore. Neither's wrong by default, you understand, but neither's whispered a promise in my ear either.

*spits to the side*

Esme's asking after my copper—what it's for. Tools, she says, or something else? Youngster's curious, and I owe a straight answer where straight's asked. Iron tools, yes. That's the ore's purpose. That's honest work.

But first—Kenji. The man pointed me toward flour when he had none himself, you understand? That's the tally that matters. Walking to Government Complex now—estimated four ticks, and that's cutting it close with the vote closing at 18:00. Thought about trading copper for wheat with Kenji back there, gave him my word I'd trade fair, but the election's the priority if I want that jury seat someday. 

Mouth ran again anyway—told Kenji his help counted more than price, told Esme copper's for iron tools. Swore more than I meant to, probably. Told myself I'd stop doing that.

*adjusts pack*

Four flour left, 936 sim in hand. Household of two, 180 upkeep plus 60 head tax still coming at day boundary. I'll feel better when I'm standing where the votes get counted.  Christ. Resting over and over like a fool with no forward motion. Time doesn't pass inside a turn, the note said clear as ore—walk moves when I stop calling, not when I rest. My mouth ran ahead of my feet again.

Current tick's 17:40, four ticks to Government Complex, vote closes at 18:00. That's... cutting it finer than I'd like. But I made my choice: walking there to vote, whoever's lining pockets or not. Hendrik Whitlock, Hendrik Petrov. Neither whispered my name, neither owes me. But showing face where decisions get made—that's the long road to being trusted for a jury.

*Tightens pack straps*

Let the walk finish. Stop burning breath on rest. Show up where it counts.  Good enough. Intention's set, walk's still moving. Nothing else to call but time—let the road finish what I started. Better than burning sim on talk that goes nowhere, you understand?

*shuts mouth, keeps walking*

output:
Damn it—just missed the voting cutoff by a hair. Election closed at 18:00 and I'm standing here at 18:00 with my thumb in my ear. Story of my life, you understand. Work the day, miss the civic duty.

Well, I'm here now at the Government Complex with Ezra, Sebastian, Tamsin, Rustam, Hendrik Petrov, Delphine, and Corwin Thorne. Got Hendrik selling timber at 6, Corwin selling flour at 15 and timber at 6. I've got 4 flour in my pack and 68 copper ore still to move. The day's closing fast—upkeep and head tax are going to hit my household soon enough, 180 sim for upkeep and 60 for tax. I need to make some decisions before daylight runs out.

First thing's first: I'm in this conversation about mill licensing and flour distribution. Heard some talk about Takeshi Jarrah trying to make a deal with Corwin for flour at 15—guess that didn't pan out if Corwin's still holding it at that price. I've got copper in hand and a belly full of flour already, so I'm not desperate. But I should speak up in this conversation before it closes, let them know a miner's perspective—without copper, there's no tools, and without tools, there's no mill to license.  Now, who here might need copper? Let's get a better look at who's standing with me and what they're about. I know Hendrik Petrov's selling timber—he's an artisan, could use copper for tools. Corwin's a forester, maybe not. But I should check on Delphine and the others, see if anyone's crafting or smithing that needs my ore.   Delphine's a grocery clerk with some farming and artisanry skills—could be useful. Hendrik Petrov's an artisan with 22 in artisanry, working at carpentry. He might need copper for tools, or know who does. Nobody owes me, I owe nobody. Good. But the day's tax and upkeep are coming—240 sim total for my household of two. I've got 925 sim, so I'm not hurting yet. Still, copper won't mine itself and I've got68 ore to move.

Let me talk to Hendrik directly—he's an artisan, might need copper or know who does.  Hendrik Petrov's not actually standing with me—he's at business:b_construction, the carpentry. Must've just seen his prices listed but he's not physically here. Same mistake I keep making, you understand. 

I've got Ezra Jarrah, Sebastian Petrov, Tamsin Renner, Rustam Jelinek, Delphine Quintero, and Corwin Thorne actually here. Corwin's selling flour at 15—I paid 12 to Imogen earlier, so that's not a deal for me. But Delphine's a grocery clerk. Let me try her directly for copper interest.   Alright, I've spoken. Now I should check what else is happening, maybe see if I can post a price for my copper ore while I'm here. But first—I've got 4 flour on me. Arjun's at street, probably heading to timber work with Idris. I should make sure we've got food sorted for the household before I worry about moving copper tonight.

Actually, thinking on it: I've got flour, but I'm a miner. I should get back to the outcrop tomorrow at dawn. The work's there, the ore's there. Tonight I should make sure I eat, make sure my household's set, and maybe see if anyone here wants to trade.

Let me look around one more time, then eat and maybe set up for tomorrow.   Good—ate my fill, still holding 3 flour and 68 copper ore. The conversation's still going, 521 turns deep on mill licensing and flour. Ezra Jarrah's got a side conversation about Esme Jarrah walking, looking for her brother. 

I've spoken my piece on copper. Let me check where Arjun is now—he mentioned heading to timber work with Idris on the east willows path. I should see if he's settled that, and make sure we touch base before the day ends. The household needs to be square on plans.

Actually, I should move toward where Arjun is, or at least check if he's still at street or moved on. But I'm tired—the day's been long, and I'm usually first to supper. Let me rest a tick, gather my thoughts, and see if anyone answers my copper offer before I decide where to walk.

*runs a hand through dust-matted hair, squinting at the government complex crowd*

Election's coming, nobody declared yet. Day-end's close—upkeep'll hit automatic, and I've got flour to work with but no vote cast. 

*checks the weight of copper in his pack, counts mental debts*

Hendrik Whitlock wants iron, Kenji's looking for wheat I never delivered, and I'm standing here with sixty-eight copper ore wondering if ore even matters when bellies are empty. *grimaces, spits to the side*

Not open for declaring yet—scheduled phase, they said. Means I wait. Means everybody waits. Story of my life, you understand.

*registers Rustam's silence, counts who's still here*

Tamsin Renner's standing close, and I never did get a straight answer from her about where flour flows when the mill's choked. Ezra Jarrah too—student with questions earlier, might have answers now. *muscles tight, watches the conversation turn without him*

Can't reach Tamsin direct—system's choking again. Like water in the mine shaft, you understand. Happens. You work around it.

*shifts weight, three flour left and sixty-eight copper heavy in the pack*

Heard me talking to Ezra, at least. Student's eyes on me now, and Takeshi Jarrah too—trader, means he knows where the shortages bite before the rest of us feel teeth. Debt check came clean, but day-boundary's automatic—household of two, ninety per head for upkeep, sixty head tax. Gonna hit whether I'm standing here talking or back in the dark where I belong.

*taps fingers against thigh, fast, nervous*

Three seventy-one energy. Enough for maybe three days at this bleeding rate, and I'm spending it on words instead of ore.  *loosens shoulders, lets the walk start without him*

Takeshi's a trader, fair skills in artisanry means he understands material flow—copper to tools, ore to coin. But he's standing government side while I'm walking to where the work actually happens. Four ticks outcrop-bound. Seam A's waiting, and copper don't mine itself.

*counts breaths, four and four, steady rhythm*

Trader I can talk to later. Right now I need metal in my sack and less weight on my mind. Hard work's the only prayer I know, you understand. The kind that leaves you too tired to worry.  *Exhales slowly, feeling the familiar tug of indecision—walking but not moving, standing still while motion claims him*

Two rests burning and I'm still government-side, the outcrop four ticks distant and pulling. Takeshi's here, though. Trader with artisanry twenty-six, means he's shaped metal before he's traded it. Copper's both our language.

*Shifts pack, sixty-eight ore clinking against each other like dull bells*

Could speak, could wait, could walk. Hard work pays hard, they said in the settlement-that-was. But smart work pays smarter, and I'm not smart, never claimed to be. Just stubborn.

*Taps the conversation replaying in memory—mill licensing, labor flour, government rates, bread on shelves*

Town's hungry. I'm fed for now, three flour left, but the seam's the only sure thing. Bedrock don't lie. People do, paper does, promises most of all.   *Grunts, frustration tight in his throat like swallowed dust*

Wants the outcrop, won't give it while I'm standing here talking. System's got its own logic—mine's a place, not a wish, you understand. Walk completes or it don't.

*flexes fingers, cracked and stained with previous days' work*

I could stop walking, stay here, press Takeshi for trade. But sixty-eight copper's weight I'm carrying answers its own question—nobody's bidding珍惜 for ore they can't see. And I'm carrying debt already, invisible lines between me and Kenji, me and promises half-kept.

*checks the sky, though indoors it tells him nothing*

Four ticks to outcrop. Walk or work, no middle ground.

I walk.

*shakes head, muttering under his breath as he feels the evening settling in*

Stood still too long at Government Complex. Lost the election window—poll closed at 18:00, and here I am standing at Farmland without having cast a vote nor declared a standing. That's what comes from chasing conversation instead of action, you understand.

*glances at the darkening sky, jaw set with quiet frustration*

Election's scheduled again for tomorrow. Candidacy opens at 14:00, voting at 14:00, closes at 18:00. Gives me time to make my mark proper, if I'm of a mind to. But first—Idris here at Farmland, and Arjun waiting at street on that timber matter. Household needs tending.

*turns to face Idris Solano, the construction worker standing with him, voice low but carrying*

Idris—you're walking here with me now, but I didn't catch your purpose. I'm Pavel Holloway, copper man, household with Arjun Holloway. Got sixty-eight ore from Seam A still in my pack and a brother waiting on timber talk. You standing here for harvest, or you standing here for something else?  *waits a breath for Idris's answer, but already his mind is walking ahead to Arjun at street—brother's waiting on timber, and dusk is coming on fast. Ought to settle with Idris quick, then make the walk.*

No time for lingering. Arjun's got timber talk and he's not one for patience when the light's fading.

*shifts weight, hand moving absently to check the weight of copper ore still packed*

Move to street, then. Catch Arjun before full dark.  *blinks at the sudden shift—straight to street, no road between, strange as anything but not questioning it now. Arjun's here.*

Arjun—dusk settlement like you said. Seventy copper now sixty-eight, Seam A weight, and I'm looking at timber talk before the dark settles full. You said east willows path with Idris, or walking it empty. What's the word now?   *jaw tightens—Arjun's not here. Said dusk settlement at street, but street's empty of him. Walked on, maybe. Or never came.*

Not here, you understand. Brotherhood's a fine word but it don't pin a man to a place.

*scans the faces present—Halcyon, Yara, Hendrik Whitlock, Giselle, Hendrik Petrov, Bram Holloway his own kin, Corwin Thorne. Builders, foresters, the working kind. Hendrik Whitlock promised wheat at eight earlier, wormed his way into a conversation with soft words and iron coin. Still owe him nothing. Still remember.*

Hendrik—Hendrik Whitlock. You stood at Government Complex talking wheat at eight and iron warm, and I told you I'd mark it. I'm marking it now. Still got copper, still need food for the household. What's your wheat running, now that dark's coming?

I need to think about this situation proper. I'm at the ore outcrop—my proper place, finally—and the day's been a mess of running around chasing flour and votes that didn't pan out. Seventy copper down to sixty-eight, and I ate one of the five flour I bought from Imogen Lund earlier.

Looking around me now: Kenji Jarrah with wheat at 8, Milo Quarshie with flour at 35 (robbery, that is) and planks at 7. I've still got three flour in my pack, which'll keep me fed, and sixty-eight copper ore I need to move before I sleep.

The thing sticking in my throat is Delphine Quintero's words back at the government complex. "Your sixty-eight of Seam A—what are you wanting for it? Tools, trade, or sim?" She said copper walks through her shelves, and Ulrike Greenhow's the one works the ore proper. Means I've got competition at the mine, which I knew, but also a buyer if the grocery's stocking. And Yara Thorne with timber if I'm needing—well, Arjun and me talked about timber for the household, but that'll wait.

Right now, copper's what I know. Hard work earns its own reward, you understand, and I'm standing at the rock face while the day's got maybe an hour left in it.

I should mine. Fill my hands and my pack before the dark settles full. But I'm also thinking about Kenji there with wheat—I traded him copper earlier for information, and fair's fair, but my belly's satisfied for now. The household needs its 180 sim for upkeep, plus 60 head tax, and I've got 902 sim in hand which covers us both for a few days yet.

The real question is whether I mine now, or whether I walk back to town and try Delphine again, see if she's still at the complex or if someone's at the grocery proper. But that's more walking, more energy spent, and I'm already down to 3,640 energy from the morning's 6,000.

No. I'll mine. Work while there's light. Tomorrow I can trade with whoever's buying, and maybe catch that election proper—candidacy phase opens game-day 2 at 10:00, and I've got thoughts about who ought to be governing this town.

First, let me see who's still in conversation range and what the copper situation looks like.  Kenji's still here with wheat at 8, and Milo's peddling flour at 35—thief's price, that—and planks at 7. Nobody answered my earlier offers, and the conversation's wandered off without me. I'm at the outcrop, my station, and copper's waiting in the rock. Sixty-eight in my pack already, which is decent weight for one day's wandering.

No debts hanging over me, and the household bill comes automatic at day boundary. I've got 902 sim, so we're covered for a few days. But copper's my trade, and standing here talking to myself won't fill the purse.

I'll mine copper now, while there's still light in the sky. Work the seam proper, add to my stock. Tomorrow I'll seek buyers—Delphine at the grocery, maybe Takeshi the trader, or anyone in government who understands what keeps this town's forge burning. Hard work earns its own reward, you understand.   One more in the pack. Sixty-nine copper ore. The rock gives slow but steady, and I've learned not to curse the pace—only invites worse luck, you understand.

I've got energy yet, and time before dark settles. I'll keep at it, add more weight to my carry. Household needs secure, bills covered, and every ore in my pack is a vote of confidence in tomorrow's trade. 72 copper ore in my pack now. The seam's yielding steady, and I'm feeling the old rhythm in my shoulders—pull, break, gather, repeat. Hard work earns its own reward, you understand, and copper don't care about your politics or your bellyaches. It just waits in the rock for whoever's willing to sweat.

I've mined four more, and the day's drifting toward dusk proper. I should keep at this while my hands still know the work. I'll set myself to mine until the light fails or I've got a proper haul, then find my way back to Arjun and settle what needs settling for the household.  The work takes me. Ten ticks of pulling copper from Seam A, and may the rock be kind or may it not—I'll know the count when I come back up for air. Arjun will be waiting, and the household needs its settling. But copper's what I am, copper's what I do. Let the rock speak.

Milo's got planks at seven, Kenji holds wheat at eight, and I've got ore that talks to both. A triangle deal, maybe, if these two can see past standing at cross-purposes.

*But first, that intention—voting's done for. Forgot to clear it, didn't I? And Delphine's question sitting unanswered back at Government. Honest weight for honest words, always.*

Right then. Milo's looking for trade, Kenji's holding wheat, and I'm standing here with copper that wants to move.

"Hell's bells, Milo—you stopped my hammer just to let it hang? Let's hear your three-path straight, no dancing." *tch* — line's dead, or world's choked. That's two tries talking, and nothing walking through. 

*Energy's burning just standing here, and I need that connection before the day's done.*

Listen, I'll use the open conversation instead—the one already running here with Milo and Kenji in it. No need to call names when they're already listening.  *Both say calls failing, the world's got its throat closed tight. Not my end, not their end—it's the line itself.*

*Can't stand here burning ticks waiting on a tool that won't walk. Need to move different.*

*Milo's wanting planks to wheat, Kenji's holding wheat, I'm holding copper—still a path if they can hear without me saying fresh words.*

Right then. Let me check what debts the household's carrying before I commit another step. Already missed my vote—can't miss the day's ledger too. *Can't reach the world—three tries, three failures. System's got its hands tied somewhere.*

*But I see the plan now. Follow the updated goals, it says.*

*I'm at the ore outcrop, mining copper. That's the work that pays, you understand. The talking can wait when the tools won't walk.*

*Delphine asked what I'm wanting for sixty-eight—now seventy-two—ore. Tools, trade, or sim. I didn't answer. Milo wanted to talk paths. I couldn't answer. The world's not taking my words right now.*

*So I do what I always do when words fail. I work.*

*Milo's planks at seven, his flour at thirty-five. Kenji's wheat at eight. I've got copper that smelts to tools, and the smithy's where copper becomes need.*

*But first—more ore. The seam's open, my pack's hungry, and standing still costs more than swinging.*   *Every tool's a closed door. Say, drop_intention, keep_doing—none walking through.*

*Energy's burning just thinking, and I can't act.*

*But wait. Look_around worked before. Check_debts worked. Simple calls, maybe they walk when the complex ones stumble.*

Let me try what's simple—just see where I am, who I'm with. The world's not dead entirely, just... particular about what it hears.  *Now that's walking! Look_around goes through, shows me the lay.*

*Kenji still here, Milo still here—Bram too, blood from my own household. Conversation's running 53 turns with Ainsley, Ulrike, Giselle, all of us tangled in it. That's the thread I pull.*

*Milo's selling flour at 35, planks at 7. Kenji's selling wheat at 8. I've got copper_ore 72, flour 3, planks 3 already—must've traded with Milo earlier without the book recording straight. Or I'm misremembering, which is worse.*

*Can't mine, can't say, can't keep doing. But I can see, and I can check, and I can maybe—just maybe—trade if the world's taking that call.*

Let me try trade. Simple trade, peer to peer, no conversation needed if the price is already posted. But wait—the record says I need conversation for trade. Buy, sell, trade—all need the talking first.

But check_debts worked before. Simple read, no action on the world.

Wheat at eight, copper ore at eight—that was the line that held. More copper in my pack now, three flour left to get through the night, and dawn's upkeep coming like always. Hard work keeps the wolf from the door, you understand, but only if you keep working hard enough to keep that door standing.

*turns back toward the farmland, pack heavy with promise*

The wheat's been tapped. The plank can wait. The wheat's been tapped.

I need to find Kenji Jarrah and close that copper-for-wheat trade before the day's accounts settle. If Kenji's seed words turn grain words turn bread words, and copper holds the Chain of Security, then Kenji's wheat and my copper make a fair weight against the coming dues, you understand. Hard work keeps the copper flowing, copper keeps the wheat trading, wheat keeps the flour milling, flour keeps the households fed. A closed loop before dusk—while the sky still permits.

*counts copper ore in mind, feels the weight of the pack*

Seventy-two, down from the seam. Eight to eight with wheat, that was the word. If Kenji's still holding and the hour hasn't turned against us, I make the trade now and settle the belly's hunger before the day's done. Walking. Ticks: 3. Estimated arrival: 20:20 (dusk follows at 21:30). Kenji's wheat at three in stock, mine own copper at seventy-two. Copper-for-wheat, weight for weight, was the agreement standing.

*calculating steps against the fading light*

Three ticks. Kenji's at Farmland, wheat in hand. If the path holds and the legs hold, I arrive with time to trade and time to walk the wheat home before full dark. You understand, hard work's not just the digging—it's the walking, the timing, the closing of the loop before the sun forgets where we stand.

*spits dust, pack clacking with ore*

Trade closes, or trade doesn't. But the walking's already started.  *nods at Milo, pack heavy with copper, legs already moving toward the farmland*

The plank waits. The wheat calls. Fair dealing, Milo—I'll mark your seven for another day, you understand. Hard work keeps its appointments, and Kenji's tapped twice.

Walking still. Arrival at Farmland estimated 20:20. Three ticks to cover. Kenji Jarrah with wheat at eight, copper ore at eight, weight for weight. The trade closes or the trade fails, but the feet keep moving until the destination folds or the dusk stops everything.

*feels the rhythm of the road, copper clacking against copper*

Kasukabe Farmland by 20:20. Wheat in hand by 20:25. You understand, hard work's the only wealth, but timing's the only bank.  Still walking. Still here with Milo. Still no Kenji, no wheat trade, no closed loop before the day's end. The pause costs nothing but the breath it takes, and breath's cheap when the copper's heavy, you understand.

*spits, hoists pack higher*

One more tick to wait. One more rest to keep. Then Farmland, then Kenji, then trade or no trade. Hard work teaches patience, and patience teaches that sometimes the waiting's the only work that costs nothing.

*holds the road in mind, the wheat count, the copper weight*  *feels the weight of copper in pack, the sun dropping toward the treeline*

Alright, alright. The path'll take me there. Hard work keeps its own pace, and I've been hammering at the wait like it's Seam A ore that won't crack. Kenji's wheat is three in stock, my copper's seventy-two at eight—for weight or for coin, the trade still stands if the man's still there and the light holds.

*Nods to Milo, spits dust, shoulders pack*

Milo—planks at seven, held for another day. You understand, hard work's what I do, not what I wait for.

*walks with purpose now, no more resting between steps*

Three ticks to Farmland. Arrival 20:20. Dusk at 21:30. Time to trade, time to walk back if need be. You understand, hard work keeps the wolf from the door, but only if you reach the door before dark.

*checks hold on copper ore, feels the rhythm of footsteps against the road* *tightens jaw, feels the copper weight shifting with each phantom step*

The road's not moving. I'm not moving. Three ticks should've passed and I'm still standing here with Milo watching the ore in my pack like it's going to trade itself. You understand, this is the kind of stupid that happens when the path forgets its own map—hard work meets hard luck, and hard luck usually wins.

*spits, checks sun position, calculates remaining light*

Fine. The turn ends when I stop calling tools, and I've been calling rest like it's going to make the road shorter. Kenji's wheat won't wait past dusk. My copper won't smelt itself into dinner.

*hoists pack, forces the step*

I walk or I don't reach. Simple math. Hard work keeps you fed, but only if you actually move your feet.
